A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, algorithms and research objectives. The main text, figures, tables and Appendices A–H are available and support comparison.

before.justification: Figure 1 presents a limited synthetic numerical illustration: wavelet reconstructions using Daubechies bases with S=1 and S=5 at resolutions J=1,...,5. The substantive research results are otherwise theoretical.

after.justification: Figure 1 retains the numerical wavelet reconstructions from v1, which still qualify as original computational outcomes. No additional empirical evaluation of the proposed online algorithms is reported.

M1.justification: The prescribed maximum wavelet depth changes from ceil(log2(T)/d) to ceil(S log2(T)/(d epsilon)), including for the local experts in Section 4.1. Coefficient updates and aggregation remain unchanged. The new nonlinear oracle is a proof device, not an implemented selection component.

E1.justification: The same one-dimensional wavelet-approximation illustration is retained. No training or evaluation datasets, domains or task scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons against the proposed online algorithms. Tables 1–2 retain the same theoretical comparators; the added citations do not introduce empirical baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 1 retains S=1 and S=5 with J=1,...,5. No experimental splits, metrics, budgets or testing procedures change. The revised algorithmic depth is not presented as a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The approximation illustrations and spatial-heterogeneity example are retained. The new nonlinear-oracle argument revises the theoretical proof; it does not add an ablation, robustness test or empirical supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 1 retains the same approximation curves, and no empirical performance scores or findings are added or revised. Changes to analytical regret bounds and complexity expressions are theoretical changes.

T1.justification: Appendix A replaces the linear-truncation argument with a nonlinear oracle combining coarse coefficients and selected fine-scale coefficients. The truncation bound changes from 2^(-sJ) to 2^(-J(s-d/p)), with new estimation and approximation bounds. Theorem 1 adds an epsilon margin and revises logarithmic-factor accounting. Appendix B adds justification for dispensing with nonlinear selection for Hölder competitors.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the constructive minimax and local-adaptivity claims. However, the contribution comparison in Table 1 adds epsilon<s-d/p as a required input alongside S and B, qualifying the previously stated parameter requirements for adaptivity.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly explains how retaining all coefficients at a large resolution increases estimation cost, motivating the nonlinear oracle. Appendix B explains why this mechanism is unnecessary for Hölder competitors. Existing discussions of spatial heterogeneity and unbounded-function limitations remain.

D1.justification: Tables 1–2 document the additional epsilon input. Appendix F specifies the partition-tree depth and expands the total computational-cost expressions, including the S/epsilon and S²/epsilon² factors associated with the revised depths.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhang et al. (2023) on online wavelet-based dynamic regret and DeVore (1998) and Donoho et al. (1996) for nonlinear approximation. Table 2 also explicitly restricts the Liautaud et al. (2025) comparison to d=1. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 expands the intuitive Besov-space explanation, clarifies the parameter-free terminology and reorganizes the exposition within Appendices A–B. It also adds brief introductions to Appendices G–H and cleans up notation, while retaining the overall section structure and narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from small vertically stacked panels beside text to a larger horizontal pair. Tables 1–2 are resized, floats are relocated, and Figure 2's caption and Table 4's headings are edited. All four figures and four tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through the revised truncation bound, explicit depth requirements and expanded proof. However, the new nonlinear-estimation inequality preceding Equation (21) appears to omit the 2^(jd/2) wavelet-scale factor present in Equation (18). Because this unresolved step supports the central minimax guarantee, the expanded argument does not establish a reliable overall quality improvement.
